items.h: U.S. prepares tariff hikes on China, the EU and 14 other economies, AP reports
items.fact: AP reported on November 24, U.S. time, citing two people familiar with the matter, that the Trump administration would soon announce plans to raise tariffs on China, the European Union, and 14 other economies over subsidized excess production. The move follows a U.S. Trade Representative investigation into industrial subsidies; the timing could still change, and the White House and USTR did not respond to requests for comment.

items.h: Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's Hodeidah port; Houthis threaten Saudi Red Sea ports
items.fact: The Saudi-led coalition said it struck Houthi military capabilities at the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah in the early hours of November 25, local time, after telling civilians to evacuate the port. The Houthis warned that if Hodeidah were attacked, they would strike Jeddah and all other Saudi Red Sea ports (Al Jazeera, The Jerusalem Post). On November 24, Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense Directorate said 11 people were injured when a Houthi attack hit the headquarters building of the Public Investment Fund, the kingdom's sovereign wealth fund, in Riyadh's financial district; the Houthis did not claim responsibility (Al-Monitor).

items.h: NBC reports Trump officials are debating whether to target Iran's top leaders
items.fact: NBC News reported on November 24, U.S. time, citing an unnamed U.S. official and a source familiar with the discussions, that Trump administration officials were debating internally whether the U.S. military should target Iran's top leaders, with supporters arguing it would help end the war. The report did not name any specific targets (via Political Wire, Antiwar.com).

items.h: China suspends part of its gallium and germanium export ban on the U.S. until January 2027
items.fact: China's Ministry of Commerce said on November 24 that it would suspend, from November 28 through January 27, 2027, Clause 2 of its Announcement No. 46 of 2024, which in principle bars exports to the U.S. of dual-use items related to gallium, germanium, antimony, and superhard materials. Clause 1, which bans such exports to U.S. military users or for military end uses, remains in force (National Business Daily, 10jqka).

items.h: U.S. jury finds Huawei guilty on 10 counts, including Iran sanctions and trade secret charges
items.fact: On November 24, a federal jury in Brooklyn found China's Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including bank fraud and sanctions violations tied to its Iran business and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, while acquitting it of racketeering conspiracy and conspiracy to obstruct justice (Reuters). Huawei's lawyer said the company would appeal, and sentencing is set for September 14, 2027.

items.h: Solomon Islands names Australia its primary security partner in a treaty barring foreign military bases
items.fact: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale signed a treaty in Canberra on November 25 under which the Solomon Islands chose Australia as its primary security partner and agreed not to host foreign military or security bases (joint statement, Australian Prime Minister's Office). Wale did not confirm whether his country's security pact with China would be renewed, and China's Foreign Ministry said on November 24 that it followed the principle of mutual respect and equality in its relations with the Solomon Islands (AP).

items.h: Polish defense ministry calls Russian drone's airspace incursion deliberate
items.fact: Poland's Operational Command said a Russian drone briefly violated Polish airspace on the night of November 23, local time, during a Russian attack on western Ukraine, and that it authorized a shootdown but did not fire after the drone turned east, citing the risk of harm to civilians (ABC, Wirtualna Polska). Deputy Defense Minister Paweł Zalewski said on November 24 that the incident was hard to see as accidental and that Polish authorities regarded it as deliberate (European Pravda).

items.h: Zelensky cites delays in delivering 48 Patriot interceptors and continuing Starshield restrictions
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in Berehove on November 24 that approval to deliver 48 Patriot interceptors, already funded through NATO's PURL mechanism, awaited only the signature of U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and confirmed that restrictions on the Ukrainian military's use of Starshield satellite communications remained in place (Kyiv Post).

items.h: Zelensky and Hungary's Magyar meet in Zakarpattia, agree on energy and other key areas
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he and Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar reached agreement on key areas of bilateral cooperation, including energy, at a meeting in Ukraine's Zakarpattia region on November 24, where they also discussed supplies of diesel and other petroleum products, expanding rail links, and rebuilding border crossings (UNN). It was the first visit to Ukraine by a Hungarian prime minister since 2015 (RBC-Ukraine).

more.t: Iran's army claimed that two tankers caught fire and came to a halt after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz on the morning of November 24; neither the ships' names nor the extent of the damage could be confirmed (Gulf News).
The Israeli military and the Shin Bet security service said on November 24 that they had killed Naim Abu Nahal, Hamas's internal security chief, in the Gaza Strip (Gulf News).

Israel's Democrats, led by Yair Golan, said on November 24 that they were halting coalition talks with Yashar, the party of former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, and Yashar said the same day that it had signed a coalition agreement with Yisrael Beytenu (The Times of Israel).

items.h: Zelensky says Ukraine sank Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi, Libya
items.fact: President Volodymyr Zelensky said on X on November 23 that Ukrainian naval drones had sunk the Russian corvette Merkury at the naval base in Benghazi, in eastern Libya, on November 22 and had also struck the cargo ship Angara (CBS, AP). Russia has not officially commented on the loss of the corvette, and Libya's government said it rejected attempts to turn the country into an arena for international conflicts (The Moscow Times).

items.h: IRGC claims three tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
items.fact: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed that three oil tankers were rocked by heavy explosions and fires after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz (Al Jazeera, November 24). The ships' names and the extent of the damage have not been disclosed.

items.h: Iran vows to use “every means” against U.S. aggression; Qatar's prime minister meets Vance and Rubio
items.fact: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called the U.S. naval blockade an “act of crime” at his weekly briefing on November 23 and said Iran would use every means to counter U.S. aggression (Euronews); he named the lifting of sanctions, an end to the blockade, and implementation of the memorandum of understanding as conditions for stability in the strait (ABC). The same day, Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met separately in Washington with Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio (AP), and told Al Jazeera the Middle East cannot withstand another escalation between the U.S. and Iran.

items.h: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia apartment building kills at least two, injures 22
items.fact: Mykhailo Semikin, head of the Zaporizhzhia regional military administration, said a Russian attack late on November 23 partially destroyed an apartment building in the city's Kosmichnyi district, killing at least two people and injuring 22, including children ages 6 and 16 (Kyiv Independent).

items.h: Zelensky asks if it's “more effective to simply admit Ukraine into NATO”; Rutte says not all allies agree
items.fact: Zelensky called for Ukraine's admission to NATO in a video address to the 72nd Annual Session of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin on November 23, and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said not all allies agree for now (Kyiv Independent). At a joint press conference with Rutte, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said it had been a mistake not to back the U.S. proposal at NATO's 2008 Bucharest summit to admit Ukraine.

items.h: Mexico says it will try “El Chapo Isidro” at home despite U.S. extradition request
items.fact: Mexican Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said on November 23 that Mexico will put Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, whom the U.S. Justice Department names as a senior Sinaloa Cartel leader, on trial in Mexico even though Washington has requested his extradition (Reuters, Al Jazeera). Mexico's Defense Ministry said four soldiers and 16 cartel gunmen were killed in the overnight operation on November 20 that led to his capture (Al Jazeera).

more.t: UN Secretary-General António Guterres, speaking on November 23 at the Bridgetown Special Summit on AI Safety in Barbados, called for a globally inclusive, principles-based multilateral framework for managing AI risks within the next year (AFP, Al Jazeera).

Kim Yo Jong, director of the General Affairs Department of the Workers' Party of Korea, denounced Switzerland in a November 24 statement for adding the Songdowon International Children's Camp to its Russia sanctions list and said she would advise the Foreign Ministry to rigorously review, within days, the withdrawal of the Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang (KCNA, as reported by SBS).

Moldova's IPN news agency, citing eyewitnesses, reported that a drone crashed and exploded near Dnestrovsc in Transnistria at about 6:45 p.m. local time on November 23, starting a fire near a gas station; the type and origin of the drone were not known (Kyiv Independent).

South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said several Russian military aircraft entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone over the East Sea on the morning of November 24 and came close to Ulleung Island, prompting Air Force fighter jets to respond, but did not violate South Korean airspace. During the incident, the Ministry of the Interior and Safety sent Ulleung County a civil defense alert reading “Russian aircraft airspace violation” at about 7:53 a.m., and North Gyeongsang Province's all-clear message wrongly called it a North Korean aircraft before the province corrected it (Seoul Shinmun, Money Today).

items.h: Bahrain says Iranian attack started fire at Sitra industrial site; IRGC claims it destroyed two U.S. radars
items.fact: Bahrain's Interior Ministry said an Iranian attack on November 21 started a fire at a civilian industrial facility on Sitra Island, and the government said it had thwarted several other attacks (Al Jazeera). Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a missile and drone strike on U.S. bases at al-Riffa and Awali that destroyed two Patriot radars, in retaliation for an attack on a radar on Hengam Island; the claim has not been verified, and Iranian state media claimed the Sitra fire was caused by a falling U.S. interceptor missile (Al Jazeera).

items.h: IRGC claims two supertankers sailing unauthorized routes hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
items.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy claimed on November 22 that two supertankers sailing unauthorized routes struck naval mines and exploded east of the Strait of Hormuz, north of Oman's Ghanam Island, and warned shipping companies to follow its navigation instructions (Xinhua, Press TV). The vessels' names and the damage have not been confirmed outside Iran.

loc.place: East of the Strait of Hormuz (north of Ghanam Island, Oman)

items.h: Russian cargo ship hit in drone attack in Gulf of Finland; Finnish military says Ukraine likely responsible
items.fact: Finland's Defense Ministry said a Russian-flagged cargo ship, the Sparta II, was hit by a drone attack on the morning of November 21 in international waters west of Gogland Island in the Gulf of Finland (Russian officials said it was bound for Kaliningrad), and the Finnish military said Ukraine was likely responsible (Reuters, AFP). The 16 crew members were evacuated; a Russian helicopter later intruded more than 4 kilometers into Finnish airspace, and Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen said the suspected violation may have been linked to rescue or tracking operations (Al Jazeera).

loc.place: Gulf of Finland (west of Gogland Island)

items.h: Iran says it held talks with Qatari mediators; Araghchi says the blockade must be lifted
items.fact: Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on November 21 that a Qatari delegation held two hours of talks with Iranian officials in Tehran on the night of November 20 but said they were not yet formal negotiations, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the blockade must be lifted “rationally” and that discussing the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz was pointless as long as Iran's demands went unmet (AFP, Reuters). President Donald Trump told Fox News the same day that he wants a “permanent” deal that keeps Iran from getting a nuclear weapon (AFP, Reuters).

items.h: Zelensky says Russia fired about 2,700 drones and 165 missiles in a week, urges U.S. to approve Patriot deliveries
items.fact: President Volodymyr Zelensky said on November 22 that Russia had launched about 2,700 attack drones, about 1,460 guided bombs, and 165 missiles over the past week, and urged Washington to approve delivery of Patriot interceptors that allies had already paid for (Al Jazeera). Early that day, a Russian strike partly collapsed an apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, and rescuers recovered two bodies (Al Jazeera).

items.h: Russian vessel at Libya's Benghazi naval base explodes in suspected sea drone attack
items.fact: Libya's eastern government said a Russian vessel docked at the Benghazi naval base to refuel and take on supplies was hit on November 22 by a suspected sea drone, causing an explosion and fire, and that it had opened a joint investigation with Russia (Reuters, Al Jazeera). An unknown number of people were injured, and no one has claimed responsibility.

items.h: Mexico captures FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive ‘El Chapo Isidro’
items.fact: Mexico's Defense Ministry and the U.S. Justice Department announced on November 21 that Mexican troops had arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” a senior Sinaloa Cartel leader on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted list, in Guasave, Sinaloa, on November 20 (U.S. Justice Department, Al Jazeera). Mexico's Defense Ministry said the operation was coordinated with U.S. intelligence agencies, and the Justice Department said U.S. agencies supported it.

items.h: Asian stocks slide amid AI bubble fears; Kospi falls as much as 5.8%
items.fact: Amid mounting fears of an AI bubble, South Korea's Kospi fell as much as 5.8 percent on November 23 and was down 3.2 percent as of 4:30 a.m. GMT, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng dropped about 0.6 percent (Al Jazeera). On November 20, the S&P 500 had fallen 3.7 percent and the Nasdaq Composite 5.3 percent (Al Jazeera).

items.h: Netanyahu and Eisenkot meet on coalition but reach no deal
items.fact: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot, who holds the mandate to form a government, met in Herzliya on November 22 but reached no deal and agreed only to meet again (Channel 12, AP). Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension (Al Jazeera).

more.t: Drone attacks blamed on the Rapid Support Forces killed at least four people in and around Khartoum and Omdurman early on November 22 (AFP), and Denise Brown, the UN humanitarian coordinator in Sudan, said a UN building was damaged while staff were inside.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun, speaking on November 21, the eve of the country's 83rd independence anniversary, demanded that Israel withdraw from all Lebanese territory and stop its attacks, and called on armed groups to hand over their weapons (AFP).

Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet on November 21 that Thailand would halt all other bilateral talks if Cambodia kept pursuing compulsory conciliation over their maritime boundary; a Permanent Court of Arbitration conciliation commission meets in Kuala Lumpur November 24–27 (The Nation).
Denmark's parliament on November 19 ratified a U.S.-Greenland-Denmark security agreement 109–0; the deal lets the United States build two bases in Greenland (Al Jazeera).
AFP reported on November 19, citing satellite imagery and expert analysis, that China is building a runway nearly 3 kilometers long on Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands.
Haitian police said they killed at least 34 suspected gang members in a November 19 operation in the Martissant area of Port-au-Prince (Reuters, AP).

Pakistani Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik arrived in New Delhi on November 20 for a Shanghai Cooperation Organization civilizational dialogue forum, becoming the first Pakistani federal minister to visit India since the May 2025 conflict, though no bilateral meeting was scheduled (Al Jazeera).

Belgian air traffic control agency Skeyes said it would be unable to provide normal service from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. local time on November 23, a national day of union action against government austerity, and nearly all flights at Belgian airports were expected to be canceled (AFP, DPA).

items.h: Two Russian cruise missiles and a suspected drone come down in southeastern Poland; NATO calls it a “grave violation”
items.fact: During a massive Russian attack on Ukraine early on November 20 (local time), two Russian cruise missiles and an object believed to be a jet-powered drone came down in Poland's southeastern Lublin and Subcarpathian provinces, with no casualties (AP, Kyiv Independent). Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it appeared Poland was dealing with an intentional provocation, and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte called it a “grave violation” of Polish airspace and said NATO jets were scrambled (AP, The Guardian).

items.h: Russia hits Ukraine with 400-plus drones and 110-plus missiles, killing at least eight
items.fact: Russia struck multiple regions of Ukraine overnight on November 19–20 (local time). President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attack involved more than 400 drones and more than 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, and killed at least eight people (AP). Russia's Defense Ministry said it hit Ukrainian military-linked sites, including a missile assembly plant (AP).

items.h: Saudi-led coalition says it struck Yemen's Hodeidah port; Houthis threaten Saudi Red Sea ports
items.fact: The Saudi-led coalition said on November 20 that it had struck facilities at Yemen's Hodeidah port used for smuggling and weapons transport. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that if the coalition hit Hodeidah, the group would target Saudi Red Sea ports including Jeddah and a power station at Shuqaiq in the south, and told airlines to avoid Saudi airspace (Al Jazeera, AFP). The coalition said it intercepted three ballistic missiles headed for Riyadh (Al Jazeera).

items.h: Estonia to close road border crossings with Russia for six months from December; Moscow objects
items.fact: Estonia's government on November 20 gave preliminary approval to closing its road border crossings with Russia for six months starting December 1; rail freight will continue under customs checks (Reuters). Estonia accused Russia earlier this month of being behind an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems, which the Kremlin denied, and Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said Moscow would take political and diplomatic countermeasures if Tallinn went ahead (Reuters).

items.h: Myanmar and China object to ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
items.fact: The International Court of Justice ruled 9–6 on November 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in its 2016–2017 crackdown, and ordered compensation and the safe return of the Rohingya (AFP, Reuters). Myanmar government spokesperson Khaing Khaing Soe said on November 20 that the ruling was not fair because it was not unanimous, and Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said such rulings do not help settle disputes (AFP, Reuters).

items.h: Trump says he and Xi will set “joint guardrails” on AI, threatens “tremendous tax” on data centers built abroad
items.fact: At a White House news conference on November 20, President Donald Trump said he and Chinese President Xi Jinping had agreed on “some joint guardrails” for artificial intelligence, without giving details, and threatened a “tremendous tax” on U.S. companies that build data centers overseas (CBS). On Iran, he said he wants a real deal rather than a fake one, and that while there is a rumor Iran is building a dirty bomb, “we will not allow that” (CBS).

more.t: Denmark said on November 20 it would expel Russia's defense attaché after its intelligence service concluded that Russian intelligence had tried, with help from a Danish gang, to assassinate a Ukrainian rapper; the Russian Embassy said Denmark had presented no evidence (AFP).

Britain and the European Union agreed at a summit in Brussels on November 20 to ease food and agricultural checks, link their emissions trading systems and let up to 100,000 people under 30 from each side live on the other side, though no document was signed and tuition fees remain unresolved (AP, Reuters).

items.h: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first three-way summit in Shenzhen; joint statement backs nuclear risk talks, more oil supply
items.fact: President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen on November 19, the first trilateral meeting among the three countries' sitting leaders (RFE/RL). The joint statement, released by the Kremlin and the White House, included the principle that there are no winners in a nuclear war, dialogue on reducing nuclear risks, expanded oil and gas supplies and UN reform, but made no mention of the Iran war (CBS, RFE/RL).

items.h: Putin rules out deals after Crimean Bridge strikes, invites European envoys to Moscow
items.fact: Putin said in Shenzhen on November 19 that after the strikes on the Crimean Bridge, Russia would respond rather than make agreements, and that it had shelved a partial ceasefire plan it had been weighing (TASS, Meduza). He said discussing European security without Europeans was pointless and that Russia would decide the format of dialogue with Ukraine once European envoys came to Moscow and set out their position (TASS, Reuters).

items.h: U.S. envoys join Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin; Kushner backs European seat at the table
items.fact: Germany, France and the United Kingdom hosted a Coalition of the Willing meeting at the Chancellery in Berlin on November 19, attended by U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. Kushner said, “We do believe that Russia having Europe at the table will be essential for ending the war” (Al Jazeera). He also claimed Russia had agreed to security guarantees for Ukraine modeled on NATO's Article 5 and that thousands of prisoners of war would return in the coming weeks; Russia has not confirmed this (United24).

items.h: Houthi missiles hit Saudi wealth fund tower in Riyadh; Saudi Arabia reports “material damage”
items.fact: Saudi authorities said a Houthi attack before dawn on November 19 caused material damage to the Public Investment Fund (PIF) tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, with no injuries (CBS, The National). The Houthis claimed on November 18 that they had fired cruise missiles at Riyadh's airport and financial center, and the Saudi-led coalition said the same day that it had struck 60 targets in Houthi-held areas of Yemen since November 17 (CBS).

items.h: Trump says he is “not rushing” on Iran, points to the new year
items.fact: Returning from China on November 19, Trump told Israel's Channel 12, “I'm not rushing to make any decisions on Iran,” adding that he would see what happens after the new year starts (CBS). A day earlier, the aircraft carrier USS George Washington left the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility, leaving the USS George H.W. Bush and USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East (CBS, ABC).

items.h: Russian daytime drone attacks on Kyiv damage Austrian and Dutch embassies
items.fact: Repeated Russian drone attacks on Kyiv during the day on November 19 killed one person, injured at least four and damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassy buildings and the windows of St. Volodymyr's Cathedral, AFP reported. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the bloc would summon Russia's envoy (United24).

items.h: Takaichi and Xi shake hands but hold no summit at APEC in Shenzhen
items.fact: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held no bilateral meeting during the APEC summit in Shenzhen, and a Japanese government official said formal talks would be difficult, the Yomiuri Shimbun reported. The two leaders shook hands at an event before the November 18 dinner, but Xi did not appear to respond when Takaichi spoke to him.

more.t: On November 19, Iran's foreign ministry spokesman dismissed as false allegations that Iran is developing chemical weapons (Times of Israel).

Reza Najafi, Iran's ambassador to international organizations in Vienna, said on November 19 that Iran would not cooperate with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) unconditionally and without limits while it is under bombardment, and would instead decide case by case (CBS).
Arthur Miller, the Pentagon's deputy comptroller, said on November 19 that the Iran war has cost more than $48 billion since February (CBS).

items.h: Trump and Putin meet at APEC in Shenzhen for the first time in 15 months; first U.S.-China-Russia summit set for November 19
items.fact: President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin each shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) dinner in Shenzhen on November 18 and then posed together for a group photo, their first face-to-face encounter since August 2025 (Euronews, AP). Xi held talks with Putin the same day, and the three leaders' first trilateral meeting is scheduled for November 19.

items.h: Saudi Arabia and Qatar condemn Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain; Qatar warns of “dangerous escalation”
items.fact: Iran's military claimed on state television on November 18 that its drones targeted Patriot air defense systems and other assets at Kuwait's Ali Al-Salem Air Base, while Kuwait and Bahrain said their air defenses responded to and intercepted the attacks. The same day, Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemned the attacks and an attack on a UAE-owned tanker, Qatar's foreign ministry called them a “dangerous escalation,” and U.S. Central Command said no U.S. personnel were injured in this week's attacks.

items.h: Russian strikes on Odesa's historic center kill four, wound 13
items.fact: Russian strikes on the southern Ukrainian city of Odesa on November 18 killed at least four people and wounded 13. Odesa regional head Oleh Kiper said three strikes hit the historic center (Al Jazeera, AFP), and President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned what he called “double-tap strikes after first responders and police officers had already arrived at the scene.”

items.h: European Commission proposes extra €45 billion loan toward Ukraine's 2027 budget gap
items.fact: The European Commission on November 18 proposed lending Ukraine an additional €45 billion to cover two-thirds of its 2027 financing gap, which the Commission estimates at about €70 billion (Kyiv Independent). The package consists of €25 billion in military support and €20 billion in budget support tied to reforms; Ukraine would repay the principal only after receiving Russian reparations, and member states still have to approve it.

more.t: Russia's Transport Ministry said train traffic on the rail section of the Crimean Bridge was temporarily suspended after a drone attack early on November 19 (TASS), and Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, confirmed the bridge had been attacked again (Kyiv Independent).
Zelensky said on November 18 that the Coalition of the Willing would meet in Berlin on November 19 to seek more support for Ukraine's air defenses and energy sector (Kyiv Independent).

In his opening statement to the IAEA Board of Governors in Vienna on November 18, Director General Rafael Grossi said North Korea had built an extension to the Yongbyon uranium enrichment facility since mid-September that appeared externally complete by late October, and said the expansion of its enrichment program “remains a cause for serious concern” (NK News).

Kim Jong Un, chairman of the State Affairs Commission, visited the Kim Jong Suk Naval University and other sites in South Hamgyong Province on November 17–18 and, on the east coast on November 18, denounced naval activity by “wicked enemies,” KCNA reported (NK News).

The UN Human Rights Office said at least 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan from January through October 2026, more than 1,630 of them in drone strikes, with Kordofan accounting for more than two-thirds of verified deaths (allAfrica).

items.h: Ukraine strikes Crimean Bridge for a second day; arch of road span collapses
items.fact: Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge for a second straight day, overnight on November 16–17 local time, and President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the attack. RFE/RL said images appeared to show that a 227-meter arch of the road span had fallen into the Kerch Strait and the rail section was damaged; Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, said the attack killed two people in Crimea.

items.h: After IRGC claims drone strike on U.S. radar in Bahrain, U.S. jets hit missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island
items.fact: The IRGC claimed on November 17 that it attacked a U.S. radar at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base with drones; U.S. Central Command said the drones were intercepted without damage. The same day, a U.S. military official said U.S. fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense, using precision munitions (The National, Iran International), and local Iranian authorities said there was no damage to residential areas or vital infrastructure.

items.h: Putin arrives in Shenzhen for APEC; Kremlin says bilateral meeting with Trump also planned
items.fact: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen, China, host of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, on November 17 (TASS). The Kremlin announced on November 16 that Putin would hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and a trilateral meeting with the Chinese and U.S. leaders, and that a bilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump was also planned.

items.h: Trump holds Quad meeting in Manila, announces Quad maritime patrol aircraft drills
items.fact: President Donald Trump arrived in Manila at 5:33 p.m. local time on November 17, held a Quad meeting with the leaders of Japan, Australia, and India, and announced that the Quad would conduct an exercise featuring maritime patrol aircraft (ABC News, AP). The same day he signed a joint trade statement with Thailand and said Thailand would remove tariffs on U.S. goods and buy $2.6 billion in U.S. farm products (AP reported the cuts would cover most goods).

more.t: Russia hit Kyiv's Southern and Northern bridges with ballistic missiles between November 16 and 17, according to President Zelensky, and the power company DTEK said strikes on the morning of November 17 left 700,000 households in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast without electricity (ISW).

Ukraine's General Staff claimed a strike on the Salavat petrochemical complex and its Unmanned Systems Forces claimed one on the Ufa refinery overnight on November 16–17, local time; Bashkortostan officials acknowledged the drone attack but said the plants were operating normally without significant damage (ISW).

Responding on November 17 to a CNN report that Iran was planning a dirty bomb or chemical attack in Washington, Trump said that if so, “they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before” (AP).

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said on November 17, at the close of the ASEAN summit, that talks on a South China Sea code of conduct were 85 to 90 percent complete; Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro had said on November 15 that three of four key issues, including whether the code would be legally binding, remained open (Philstar).

items.h: CENTCOM says a third U.S. carrier, the Theodore Roosevelt, has reached the Middle East
items.fact: The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East, U.S. Central Command said on social media on November 16, according to the AP, joining the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington and bringing the number of carriers in the region to three. Citing the Navy, the AP said 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship are in the Arabian Sea, with two more destroyers in the Red Sea.

items.h: IRGC claims two tankers hit mines in Hormuz; UKMTO reports a tanker struck by a projectile
items.fact: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed through state media on November 16 that two oil tankers had hit mines and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz, and that six tankers had caught fire in similar incidents on November 15–16 (Reuters). The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said the same day that a tanker leaving the strait was hit by an unknown projectile, starting an engine-room fire, with no injuries.

items.h: CNN: U.S. intelligence sees signs of an Iranian ‘dirty bomb’ plot in Washington; White House sees no credible threat
items.fact: CNN reported on November 16, citing seven U.S. officials, that U.S. intelligence has picked up signs that Iran is planning a “dirty bomb” or chemical attack in Washington targeting senior Trump administration officials, though the intelligence does not point to an imminent attack. The White House said there are currently no credible threats to the homeland, and Iran’s U.N. mission called the allegations fabricated.

items.h: EU sanctions nearly 50 Russian banks as Kallas says “Russia is really escalating”
items.fact: At a foreign ministers’ meeting in Brussels on November 16, the EU sanctioned nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, several energy-linked businesspeople and dozens of people accused of spreading pro-Russian propaganda and disinformation (AP). Member states accused Russia of dragging out talks while bombing power plants, and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said, “We see that Russia is really escalating.”

items.h: Trump on Kim Jong Un: “He may come … That’s up to President Xi”
items.fact: Leaving the White House on the morning of November 16 (local time), President Donald Trump said he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his trip to China: “He may come. I don’t know. That’s up to President Xi,” ABC News reported. There was no reported response from North Korea.

items.h: Jo Yong Won meets Putin in Moscow, denounces U.S. ‘hostile policy’ toward North Korea at forum
items.fact: Jo Yong Won, a Workers’ Party secretary and close aide to Kim Jong Un, met President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on November 16 and conveyed Kim’s best wishes, TASS reported. At an international forum in Moscow the same day attended by delegates from more than 70 countries, he denounced what he called the United States’ “chronic hostile policy” toward North Korea, according to KCNA, citing TASS.

more.t: Ukrainian regional officials said Russian attacks on November 16 killed three people, one each in Sadove, in the Kherson region; Dnipro; and Bilenke, in the Zaporizhzhia region (Al Jazeera).

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected the expansion project at Samjiyon Airport near the Chinese border and tourism construction sites around Mount Paektu on November 15–16, ordering that the airport be brought up to International Civil Aviation Organization standards, KCNA reported on November 17.
U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres said on November 16 that the United States and Iran need a serious diplomatic process to end their “neither peace nor war” situation (Iran International).
The Israeli military claimed on November 16 that its air force struck a weapons shipment bound for Hezbollah overnight near Janta, Lebanon (Iran International).

Bahrain’s public prosecutor’s office said on November 16 that a court had sentenced defendants in a case involving a group linked to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard to terms ranging from 15 years to life (Iran International).

items.h: China confirms Xi–Trump–Putin summit in Shenzhen on November 19
items.fact: China’s Foreign Ministry announced on November 16 that President Xi Jinping would host a three-way summit with the Russian and U.S. leaders in Shenzhen on November 19. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the date on November 14; China did not disclose an agenda, while the White House said nuclear proliferation would be discussed.

items.h: IRGC claims another attack on a U.S. radar in Bahrain; Bahrain’s military says it intercepted Iranian attacks
items.fact: The aerospace force of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed that on November 15 it hit a U.S. air-defense radar at the Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain with six drones. The Bahrain Defence Force said it had intercepted and destroyed several Iranian airborne attacks, and Bahrain’s Foreign Ministry said Iran bore full responsibility for the November 13 and 15 attacks and urged the UN Security Council to act.

items.h: Zelensky says the U.S. asked whether Ukraine would leave Donbas if it joined NATO
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told reporters on November 13 that the Americans had asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from Donbas if it joined NATO, adding that “NATO is back on the agenda” (remarks released by his office on November 14). He signaled he would consider a referendum only once security guarantees and other conditions were all in place.

items.h: Estonia plans to close road crossings with Russia after sabotage attempt against a drone maker
items.fact: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on November 15 that Estonia plans to close its road border crossings with Russia starting December 1 in response to a sabotage attempt against drone maker Threod Systems ordered by Russia’s GRU military intelligence. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said the ministry would check whether the reports were true.

items.h: Drones hit three merchant ships off Romania’s Sulina, two of them inside Romanian waters
items.fact: Drones struck three merchant ships in the Black Sea near Romania’s Sulina Canal on the evening of November 14 (local time), and Romanian Defense Minister Ștefan Radu Oprea said two of them, the Greek-flagged Evia Petrol V and the Marsol, flagged in St. Kitts and Nevis, were inside Romanian territorial waters. No one was injured, and the attacker has not been identified.

items.h: Pro-government southern forces in Yemen announce withdrawal from the Bab el-Mandeb area
items.fact: The Southern Armed Forces, which fight alongside Yemen’s government, announced on November 15 that they would withdraw from Dhubab airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area west of Taiz. They said their priority was defending Aden and breaking the Houthi siege of Taiz.

items.h: Ethiopian army chief says Tigray offensive was led by Eritrea and backed by Egypt
items.fact: Birhanu Jula, chief of general staff of Ethiopia’s armed forces, claimed at a press conference on November 14 that the offensive by Tigrayan rebels had been led by Eritrea and that Egypt had provided logistics and military supplies. Anadolu Agency said it could not independently verify the claims, and Eritrea and Egypt did not immediately respond.

more.t: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told a news conference on November 15 that Iran would not leave any attack unanswered, and IRNA reported that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi was scheduled to visit Muscat, Oman, on November 17.
The Saudi-led coalition said that on November 15 it intercepted two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis toward Riyadh and downed several drones over eastern areas and elsewhere.

Ukraine’s air force said Russia attacked with 132 drones starting at 6 p.m. local time on November 14 and that 106 had been shot down or suppressed as of 8 a.m. on November 15, while Russia’s Defense Ministry claimed on the morning of November 16 that it had downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on November 15 that the EU’s Operation Irini in the Mediterranean boarded the MIDAG, a tanker suspected of belonging to Russia’s shadow fleet, on November 13 and confirmed it was sailing under a false flag (Kyiv Independent).

The Israeli military said it carried out an airstrike in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis in Gaza on November 14 targeting a senior commander in Hamas’s armed wing, and Hamas’s Qassam Brigades confirmed on November 15 that Rafah Brigade commander Samir Abu Younis had been killed.

Sudan’s army said it seized several areas around al-Khuway in West Kordofan on November 13 and deployed troops in places including Suraif Ankoush, and claimed it had shot down a drone that crossed from Ethiopia into the Dandro area of Blue Nile state the same day (Anadolu Agency).
At least 1,167 people were killed and 459 injured in violence in Haiti from July to September, according to a report by the UN Integrated Office in Haiti, known as BINUH (UN News, November 12).

Myanmar’s state media claimed the army had captured the National Unity Government’s special region command headquarters, a Karen National Liberation Army battalion headquarters, and 10 other bases on the Mon–Bago border in a six-day operation (AP, reported November 10).

An ambush claimed by the Pakistani Taliban (TTP) killed 10 police officers in Kohat, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, on November 11, and authorities said 18 militants were also killed (Long War Journal).

Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev met in Dublin on November 12 on the sidelines of the European Political Community summit and discussed the Trump Route (TRIPP), power-grid links, border delimitation, and water cooperation; there were no reports of a new agreement being signed (OC Media).

Somalia’s opposition Somali Future Council said it would boycott the election talks President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud convened for November 14, citing the lack of mediation by the United States, Britain, the EU, and Turkey (Garowe Online).

items.h: Trump to meet Xi and Putin in Shenzhen next week; White House says nuclear arms cuts on the agenda
items.fact: The White House said President Donald Trump will hold a three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of next week’s APEC summit in Shenzhen, and assistant White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said he “will discuss reducing nuclear weapons” (Anadolu Agency, reported November 14). A senior U.S. official said Washington does not expect an agreement, calling the meeting “the entry point, the first conversation” at the leader level.

items.h: IRGC claims it hit a U.S. radar in Bahrain; CENTCOM says it downed two drones, with no damage
items.fact: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain on November 13 in retaliation for a November 12 attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik (Drop Site News). U.S. Central Command denied the claim, saying U.S. forces shot down two one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain and that there were no injuries or damage (Fox News).

items.h: Iran tells IAEA it won’t resume monitoring talks, citing “threats” from the U.S. president
items.fact: Iran told the International Atomic Energy Agency in a letter that monitoring talks cannot proceed amid “a series of persistent, explicit, and public threats by the President of the United States of America,” according to a confidential IAEA report sent to member states on November 13 and cited by The Associated Press. The report voiced growing concern about the Isfahan fuel enrichment plant, saying the agency does not know its exact location or whether it holds nuclear material.

items.h: Turkey and Qatar sign mutual defense pact
items.fact: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Qatar’s emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, signed five agreements, including a mutual defense pact, on November 13 at the 12th Turkey-Qatar High Strategic Committee meeting at the Dolmabahçe presidential office in Istanbul (Anadolu Agency, Khaleej Times). Erdoğan said Turkey will keep working with Doha to prevent a return to war (Khaleej Times).

more.t: The navy of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed November 13 that a liquefied natural gas carrier on an “unauthorized and dangerous route” in the Strait of Hormuz had hit a naval mine and exploded (Reuters; unconfirmed).

Israel’s Channel 12 reported that caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Prime Minister-designate Gadi Eisenkot on November 12 and discussed a possible resumption of strikes on Iran (Anadolu Agency).
Pakistan’s military said it killed 74 militants over the past 10 days in northwestern and southwestern regions bordering Afghanistan (AP, reported November 13).

items.h: Putin meets U.S. envoys; Kremlin says what could be a record prisoner swap is in the works
items.fact: After Russian President Vladimir Putin met U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at the Kremlin on November 12, presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said the talks would continue and that the terms of what would likely be the largest prisoner exchange to date are being finalized. Witkoff said, “We’ve set a new meeting.”

items.h: Zelensky says Starshield speed cap is back; SpaceX official says “this is false”
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on November 12 that the Starshield satellite terminals used by Ukraine’s military are being systematically capped at 161 km/h (100 mph), making Russian jet-powered drones far harder to intercept. A SpaceX official told the U.S. outlet TWZ, “This is false,” and “There has been no change.”

items.h: Trump says the U.S. doesn’t need an Iran deal; on force, “it’s possible I would do it right now”
items.fact: President Donald Trump posted on social media on November 12 (U.S. time): “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed.” The same day, asked by a Salem News Channel host what he would do if Iran threatened U.S. allies and ships, he said that if he saw things going the other way he would act, and “it’s possible I would do it right now.”

items.h: CENTCOM dismisses report it advised Israel to prepare for renewed Iran operations
items.fact: Israeli public broadcaster KAN, citing a U.S. official, reported that U.S. Central Command advised Israel to prepare for a possible resumption of military operations against Iran in the near future. In comments to Anadolu Agency published November 13, a CENTCOM official dismissed the account as “pure speculation” and said there had been no change to the U.S. force posture in the region.

items.h: Kremlin points to first-ever three-way summit China is planning in Shenzhen
items.fact: Presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said on November 12 that a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and President Donald Trump is planned on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, and that he hopes the trilateral summit China is organizing there, the first of its kind, will help stabilize the international situation. The Kremlin did not name the three parties; Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on November 10 that a U.S.-China-Russia leaders’ meeting on the APEC sidelines “should be possible” (Reuters).

items.h: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns as CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief
items.fact: Nvidia announced on November 12 (U.S. time) that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, and that CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her current role. The company gave no reason, and the board has begun a search for a permanent CEO.

more.t: The ninth European Political Community summit met in Dublin on November 12. Speaking there, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is trying to get details on the Starshield limits from the American side, “but so far, we know very little” (Ukrinform).

items.h: U.S.-brokered Abu Dhabi talks yield a deal in principle on a prisoner swap, no breakthrough
items.fact: Two days of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi ended November 11 with Ukraine's chief negotiator, foreign intelligence chief Rustem Umerov, and Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky saying the sides had agreed in principle on a large-scale prisoner exchange. There was no major progress toward ending the war, and U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner (President Donald Trump's son-in-law) are set to meet President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on November 12.

items.h: Ghalibaf says Iran and Oman set the rules in Hormuz; Vance reported to weigh meeting Rezaei
items.fact: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf told Al Jazeera in an interview published November 11 that the Strait of Hormuz is “governed by the laws of the two littoral states that border it,” Iran and Oman, and repeated that the U.S. must lift its blockade and sanctions, among other conditions, before talks can begin. The same day, The Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance was considering a face-to-face meeting with Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, and that the discussions were preliminary.

items.h: Trump says he wants “a total victory, not a 93 percent victory” in Iran, says ending the war is “just a question of when”
items.fact: Speaking at Arlington National Cemetery on Veterans Day, November 11, President Donald Trump said of the Iran war, “We won,” and that it was “just a question of when we want to end it.” He added: “We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93 percent victory.”

items.h: Eisenkot urges Netanyahu in a letter to hold off on “dangerous moves” until a new government is in place
items.fact: Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming Israel's next government, wrote to caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on November 11 urging him to refrain from dangerous moves that can wait until a new government is sworn in. Gulf News, citing Israeli media, reported that Netanyahu had pushed for action against Iran despite objections from IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir, a claim that has not been confirmed.

items.h: Taiwan's defense minister says China ran “area denial drills” in the western Pacific with the Liaoning carrier group
items.fact: Taiwanese Defense Minister Wellington Koo told reporters at the Legislative Yuan in Taipei on November 10 that China “has indeed conducted area denial drills in the Western Pacific” with the Liaoning carrier group and other formations, Reuters reported. National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu had said that as of November 3 more than 100 Chinese navy and coast guard vessels were deployed across the western Pacific. China has not formally announced the drills.

items.h: Indonesian Vice President Gibran hands his resignation to the MPR a day after House factions moved to impeach him
items.fact: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka delivered his resignation to leaders of the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR) at the parliament complex in Jakarta on the morning of November 12, local time, Antara reported. A day earlier, every faction in the House of Representatives had submitted a motion invoking the House's right to express an opinion, the first step toward impeachment.

more.t: Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles shortly after 1 a.m. local time on November 12, hours after the Abu Dhabi talks ended, according to the Kyiv Post.

The Saudi-led coalition said November 11 that it intercepted five missiles and two drones fired by the Houthis toward Riyadh and the kingdom's western and southern regions. Saudi civil defense said debris from ballistic missiles fell on the village of Sabuhah in the Mecca region, Gulf News reported.

Al Jazeera reported November 11 that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed three tankers caught fire after hitting mines on an “unauthorized route” in the eastern Strait of Hormuz; the claim could not be independently verified.

The leaders' segment of the UN climate conference, COP31, opened a two-day run in Antalya, Turkey, on November 11, with more than 70 world leaders and senior officials scheduled to speak, AP reported.

items.h: Rubio says strikes on Iran are unnecessary if economic pressure achieves the same goal; Iran's Rezaei denies talks
items.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Paris on November 10 after a G7 foreign ministers' meeting, said there was no need to strike Iran: “We don't need to conduct military strikes if we're achieving the same objective through economic means and economic pressure.” The same day, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called reports of talks with Washington “complete lies” in a broadcast interview and said the Strait of Hormuz would stay closed until all seven of Iran's conditions were met, according to Anadolu.

items.h: U.S.-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi run about four hours on day one; Rubio says they appear to have been “very productive”
items.fact: Russian and Ukrainian delegations met for about four hours in Abu Dhabi on November 10 in talks mediated by the United States, with a second day set for November 11, the AP reported. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the session constructive and quite substantive and said it covered prisoner exchanges, the return of detained civilians and of children deported from Ukraine, and security guarantees.

items.h: Tanker struck northeast of Lima, Oman; ship attacks around Hormuz hit a wartime monthly high of 37 in October
items.fact: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center (UKMTO) said a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile in waters northeast of Lima, Oman, on November 10 but did not say who was responsible. Reuters reported that, according to the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, 37 ships were attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz in October, the most in any month since the war began, and that 10 more attacks had been recorded so far in November.

items.h: Indonesian Vice President Gibran offers his resignation to Prabowo
items.fact: State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi said on November 10 that Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka had offered his resignation during a meeting of more than two hours with President Prabowo Subianto. It was not disclosed whether Prabowo had accepted it. Gibran has been under pressure since a court found that his educational documents did not meet the eligibility requirements to run in the election.

more.t: Russia launched 163 drones and one Kh-59/69 guided missile at Ukraine between 6 p.m. on November 10 and 8 a.m. on November 11, local time, Ukraine's air force said, adding that 144 drones were shot down or suppressed and 17 locations were hit.
Russia's oil refining capacity has fallen by about 30 percent since late October because of renewed Ukrainian drone attacks, Reuters reported, citing industry sources.

Qatar's Foreign Ministry said at a press briefing in Doha on November 10 that it was receiving positive responses from both Washington and Tehran on a diplomatic solution and that negotiations were making progress, though it could not assess how close a deal was.

items.h: Trump says "Iran militarily is effectively over" after meeting Qatar's prime minister, but keeps blockade
items.fact: President Donald Trump, after meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House on November 9, said there was momentum toward ending the war but that the naval blockade would remain in place. On Truth Social, he said renewed strikes were quite unlikely. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called it fake news about imaginary talks.

items.h: China extends rare earth export control pause to January 10, 2027, and delays other countermeasures
items.fact: China's Commerce Ministry said in a short statement on November 9 that it would extend by two months, to January 10, 2027, its suspension of the export controls on rare earths and other materials that it expanded in October 2025. Reuters reported that the move was part of a wider extension, announced the same day, of China's suspension of trade countermeasures and tariffs.

items.h: U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi, the first since February in Geneva
items.fact: U.S.-brokered three-way talks with Russia and Ukraine were set to resume in Abu Dhabi on November 10, TASS reported. TASS said presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky leads the Russian delegation and that the three sides last met in Geneva on February 18.

items.h: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for supermarket cyberattack, summons envoy
items.fact: Paris prosecutors said on November 9 that Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind the October 12 cyberattack that remotely tampered with refrigeration systems in French supermarkets, and sought international arrest warrants for the leaders of the affiliated Shahid Kaveh group. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's ambassador was being summoned and that sanctions would be imposed at the European level.

items.h: GOP Rep. Massie files impeachment articles against Hegseth over the Iran war
items.fact: Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, on November 9 filed eight articles of impeachment accusing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth of, among other things, abusing his powers and illegally waging war on Iran. Euronews reported that a vote could come as early as November 11. Trump said on November 9 that he backed Hegseth.

more.t: The UN climate conference, COP31, opened in Antalya, Turkey, on November 9 and runs through November 20; the AP reported that the U.S. was again absent.

items.h: Herzog taps Eisenkot to form Israel's next government; 46 lawmakers backed Netanyahu
items.fact: Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government on November 8 at the President's Residence in Jerusalem. Sixty-seven lawmakers recommended Eisenkot and 46 recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Eisenkot has 28 days, which can be extended by 14.

items.h: Rubio calls Iran's demands "outrageous"; Araghchi says "it is the White House's turn to choose"
items.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on November 8 pointed to Iran's two-day plan, under which the U.S. would carry out agreed measures on the first day and Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz on the second. "American voters have made their choice. Now it is the White House's turn to choose," he said. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the same day that he would not say the two sides were on the verge of a breakthrough, calling Iran's demands outrageous and unrealistic.

items.h: CENTCOM launches "Iron Gate" task force to block Iran's land and Caspian trade
items.fact: U.S. Central Command said on November 7 it had launched Task Force Iron Gate to cut off advanced weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue moving across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM also said U.S. aircraft struck and stopped the cargo ship Huda in the Gulf of Oman the same day after it ignored warnings.

items.h: Trump says Ukraine will likely "end up with a little bit different shape" ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
items.fact: In a CBS "60 Minutes" interview that aired on November 8, President Donald Trump said Ukraine would likely "end up with a little bit different shape" after the war and that a deal was very close. The Kremlin had earlier said three-way talks among the U.S., Russia and Ukraine would be held in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11.

items.h: Russia strikes Ukraine's grid, Black Sea ports; more than 600,000 lose power in Dnipropetrovsk
items.fact: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 164 drones and three missiles between 6 p.m. on November 7 and 8 a.m. on November 8 local time, and that 137 drones were shot down or neutralized. DTEK said more than 600,000 residents in the Dnipropetrovsk region lost power, and Russia's Defense Ministry claimed it hit three cargo ships around Odesa, a claim that could not be verified.

items.h: Japan seeks equal treatment for Takaichi at APEC; formal summit with China unlikely, Bloomberg says
items.fact: Bloomberg reported on November 9, citing people familiar with the matter, that Japan has asked China to confirm Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will be treated like other leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on November 18–19. A formal Japan-China summit is unlikely, with no more than a handshake expected, the report said.

items.h: China's factory-gate prices rise 5.7 percent in October; consumer prices up 0.7 percent
items.fact: China's National Bureau of Statistics said on November 9 that the producer price index rose 5.7 percent in October from a year earlier and the consumer price index rose 0.7 percent. Investing.com said the producer price increase was the fastest since June 2022.

more.t: Houthi rebels fired missiles at Riyadh on the morning of November 8, and an Aramco building in the King Abdullah Financial District was damaged; Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said falling debris caused minor damage and there were no casualties.
IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said on November 7 that Iran has lifted its self-imposed 2,000-kilometer limit on missile range.

A drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field in Iraq's Kurdistan region at 11 p.m. local time on November 8 cut gas supplies to power plants; a Kurdistan Regional Government electricity spokesman said 2,500 to 2,800 megawatts of generating capacity was lost. No group has claimed responsibility.

Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the Kirishi refinery in Russia's Leningrad region overnight on November 8–9; Governor Alexander Drozdenko said 113 drones were downed and that the Kirishi industrial zone was hit.

The Russian-installed management of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant said on November 8 that the plant lost its external power line and is running on diesel generators; Ukraine's nuclear operator Energoatom said it was the plant's 16th loss of off-site power this year.

The State Department on November 5 sanctioned two individuals, eight entities including two Chinese companies, and five vessels over the Cuban regime's foreign military support and illicit revenue networks; China's Commerce Ministry objected on November 7.

Mexico's navy said it arrested Rafael Álvarez, the alleged leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel cell "Los Rs," in Zapopan, Jalisco, on November 8, using intelligence from the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration.
Military sources told Anadolu that Sudan's army and the Joint Force took Ayyal Bakhit in West Kordofan on November 7.

Citing local sources, the U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs said at least 30 civilians were killed in an attack in the Beni area of the Democratic Republic of the Congo overnight on November 5–6; local authorities blamed the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF).

Haitian police said Mathias Saintil, leader of the Boston gang in Cité Soleil, was neutralized by gunfire, while a Haitian rights group said he died on November 6 after a drone strike the night before.
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on November 6 that Armenia's interest in the Collective Security Treaty Organization has run its course.
In Somalia, Ibrahim Idle Suleiman was sworn in as the new head of the Supreme Court at the presidential palace on November 7; the opposition Somali Future Council called it a "coup" on November 8.
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said on November 8 that Israel will not withdraw from its security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, according to AFP.

items.h: Trump says U.S. knocked out Iranian anti-aircraft device "in about 15 minutes, maybe five" in first strike since midterms
items.fact: President Donald Trump said on November 6 local time that U.S. forces had hit an anti-aircraft device Iran built, calling the strike "minor." Iranian state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island. The AP said it was the first U.S. strike since the midterms; the extent of the damage was unclear.

items.h: Qatar proposes two-day bridge deal; Iran reviewing it, Mideast officials say
items.fact: Two Middle East officials told the AP on November 6 that Qatar has proposed a plan under which, on day one, the U.S. would lift its naval blockade and return some of Iran's frozen funds and Iran would allow IAEA inspections of bombed facilities, and on day two Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. They said Iran is reviewing the plan. The White House declined to comment.

items.h: Russia hits Kyiv with ballistic missiles; Northern Bridge damaged, five injured
items.fact: Ukraine's air force said Russia attacked across Ukraine with missiles, including ballistic missiles, and 172 Shahed-type drones starting at 6 p.m. local time on November 6. As of 9 a.m. on November 7, it had shot down or neutralized four missiles and 149 drones, and the attack was continuing. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern Bridge was damaged and closed to traffic in both directions, and that five people, including a 14-year-old girl, were injured.

items.h: New Zealand early count puts National-led governing coalition on track for majority
items.fact: With 10 percent of the vote counted in New Zealand's November 7 election, National had 31.2 percent, Labour 28.3 percent, ACT 11.3 percent and NZ First 9.7 percent, with the Greens at 12.7 percent, putting the governing coalition on track for a majority, AAP reported. Official results are due by November 27.

more.t: A crew member was killed in an explosion aboard the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Velos Sapphire on November 5; the operator suspects a missile strike, but the cause has not been confirmed, Reuters reported on November 6. The International Maritime Organization said at least 25 seafarers have been killed in the Strait of Hormuz in the conflict.

At least 30 people were killed in an attack on a market in Yemen's Taiz province on November 6, Houthi health officials told the AP. The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia; authorities aligned with the Saudi-backed government blamed the Houthis.

David Arakhamia, the ruling party's parliamentary leader, confirmed on November 6 that Rustem Umerov will lead Ukraine's delegation at upcoming trilateral U.S.-Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

Elon Musk on November 5 reposted on X, without comment, another user's post saying it was a mistake for SpaceX to give Ukraine thousands of Starlink terminals and service for free, the Kyiv Independent reported on November 7.

items.h: Iran's Rezaei: no Hormuz reopening, no talks until U.S. meets seven conditions
items.fact: Iran has sent the U.S. a nuclear proposal through Qatar but will discuss it only after Washington meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions, returning frozen assets and paying war reparations, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on November 5. Mohsen Rezaei, Iran's top security official, made the same point while visiting Russia.

items.h: Nasdaq plunges 5.5 percent into correction on fears of Democratic AI curbs
items.fact: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52 percent to close at 24,315.00 on November 5, entering correction territory, while the S&P 500 lost 4.36 percent, the Seoul Economic Daily reported. The selloff was blamed on fears that Democrats, after winning control of Congress, will tighten rules on AI and data centers.

items.h: Iran claims a string of tankers hit mines near Hormuz
items.fact: Iran's military and the Revolutionary Guards said on November 5 that tankers and a tugboat caught fire after mine strikes and other incidents in waters south and east of the Strait of Hormuz. Taken together, the Iranian statements claim at least five tankers and one tug; none of the claims has been independently verified. January Brent futures settled up 3.88 percent at $98.29 a barrel that day, according to the Seoul Economic Daily.

items.h: Melania Trump hosts Russian, Ukrainian officials: "something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire"
items.fact: Melania Trump met Kirill Dmitriev, President Vladimir Putin's special envoy, and Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's parliamentary human rights commissioner, among others, at the White House on November 5 to mark a six-day truce in Oleshky, in the Kherson region, that ended November 1, and the evacuation of nearly 800 residents. President Donald Trump told reporters it would be "a big agreement" that "might involve all of Europe."

items.h: Somalia's top court rules term extension unlawful; president announces chief justice's dismissal
items.fact: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on November 5 that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension was unlawful and ordered a new agreement among political parties within 30 days and elections within 90, AFP reported. Before the ruling was published, the presidency announced it was dismissing Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed.

more.t: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigned on November 5 amid the bankruptcy of digital bank Ueno; the Chamber of Deputies voted unanimously to impeach him, and Vice President Pedro Alliana will succeed him, Euronews reported.

Hoax bomb threats targeted at least 27 European passenger flights from Ireland to Bulgaria on November 5, the second such wave this week, and some made unscheduled landings, Hong Kong's The Standard reported.

The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said on November 5 that a tanker was struck by two projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash-Shamal, Qatar, at 11:20 p.m. GMT on November 4 (2:20 a.m. November 5 local time).

items.h: Oil plunges more than 8 percent after U.S. midterms; Brent at $94
items.fact: Brent fell 8.6 percent to $94.66 a barrel as of 1:06 p.m. ET on November 4, with WTI at $88.08, according to OilPrice.com. With Democrats now controlling both chambers of Congress, markets are trying to gauge where the U.S.-Iran war is headed, The National reported.

items.h: Vance blames Iran war for GOP midterm losses
items.fact: Vice President JD Vance wrote on X that the Iran war cost Republicans in the midterms and that "any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there," OilPrice.com reported on November 4.

items.h: Zelensky tells Witkoff, Kushner postwar guarantees must be ironclad
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he spoke for about 90 minutes on November 4 with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about Patriot interceptors and postwar security guarantees. In Brussels the same day, the U.S., Ukraine, NATO, Germany, France and the U.K. coordinated positions ahead of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11.

items.h: Indonesia's military mobilizes thousands in capital after presidential wiretap case
items.fact: Indonesia's military said it was mobilizing thousands of troops to tighten security in the capital after President Prabowo Subianto on November 4 fired his chief of staff, Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who had been arrested on suspicion of illegally wiretapping the president and others, Reuters reported. A presidential spokesman said the conduct could border on treason.

items.h: South Korea's Defense Ministry seeks to widen Cheonghae Unit zone south of Oman
items.fact: A revised Defense Ministry motion extending the Cheonghae Unit's deployment cleared a vice-ministerial meeting on November 5, SBS reported. It widens the unit's zone from the Gulf of Aden to south of Oman's port of Duqm and adds a P-8 maritime patrol aircraft, an explosive ordnance disposal team and unmanned mine-countermeasure systems. A ministry official said direct detection of the Strait of Hormuz or Iranian territory would be limited, Financial News reported.

more.t: Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, was quoted as saying that anyone expecting a shift in U.S. policy after the midterms is badly mistaken, The National reported on November 4.

The death toll from the November 2 bombing of a school used as an aid-distribution point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 40, local officials said on November 4. Zelensky said more than 30 people may be trapped under the rubble.

Kyiv's water utility said Russia's November 3 strikes on energy infrastructure effectively cut off the city's water supply. Experts and sources called it the worst outage since the full-scale war began.

KCNA reported on November 5 that North Korea had tested a surface-to-air missile with a new guidance system and a cruise missile that drops cluster munitions on runways the previous day, NK News said.

items.h: Democrats retake Senate, projected to win House in U.S. midterms
items.fact: Democrats flipped Republican-held Senate seats in North Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Kansas, Iowa and South Carolina in the November 3 midterms, winning control of the chamber, the AP reported. NBC, CNN and others projected that Democrats would also win a House majority, but the AP had not called the House as of late November 3.

items.h: Russia pounds Ukraine's grid; Kyiv says drones targeted nuclear-plant substation
items.fact: Ukrainian Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said Russia hit power plants and substations with 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles starting early on November 3, sending three drones toward a substation critical to the stable operation of the Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plant, and that Ukraine had notified the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). Grid operator Ukrenergo imposed emergency blackouts in Kyiv and several other regions.

items.h: Trump confirms strike on Iranian air-defense site, calls it a "minor attack"
items.fact: President Donald Trump said in a Fox News interview on November 3 that Iran had built an anti-aircraft facility and that "as soon as it was completed, we hit it last night," calling it a "minor attack." A U.S. official told the AP on November 2 that U.S. forces had struck Iranians who used surface-to-air missiles against them in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island and elsewhere, and Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran had a legitimate right to self-defense.

items.h: Trump says he and Netanyahu agreed to end U.S. aid to Israel by year's end
items.fact: Trump said in a Fox News interview on November 3 that the U.S. gives Israel $4 billion a year but that he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "made a deal months ago that we're stopping," adding that "by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel." The current memorandum of understanding provides about $3.8 billion a year over 10 years starting in 2019; Netanyahu has previously spoken of phasing out aid over a decade, and his office did not immediately comment.

more.t: The White House said on November 3 that first lady Melania Trump will host Russian and Ukrainian representatives on November 5 for an event where she will speak about a localized ceasefire and civilian evacuation operation in Oleshky, in the Kherson region.

Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari said, "We remain hopeful that there is still a chance for a deal" between the U.S. and Iran, adding that Qatar was working toward an interim agreement.

items.h: Russian bombs hit aid-distribution school in Zaporizhzhia region; Ukraine says 26 killed
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on November 2 that a school distributing humanitarian aid in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, and a shelter inside it were hit one after another by Russian aerial bombs, killing 26 people, and that nine more bombs fell after the first strike. Regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said 27 people were missing.

items.h: U.S. plans three-way talks with Russia, Ukraine in Abu Dhabi November 10–11, senior official says
items.fact: A senior U.S. official told Reuters on November 2 that the U.S. will hold three-way talks with Ukrainian and Russian delegations in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11 on postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures and ending the war. Special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to represent the U.S., the official said.

items.h: Iranian negotiators leave Doha as draft deal circulates; Iran ties final deal to blockade's end
items.fact: Iranian negotiators left Doha, where they had been meeting Qatari mediators, on November 1, but not because the talks had stalled, an official briefed on the negotiations told Reuters on November 2. A draft deal with the U.S. is circulating and a follow-up meeting is possible, the official said. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said there will be no final deal and no reopening of the strait until the U.S. naval blockade ends and Iran's demands are met.

more.t: A local ceasefire around Oleshky in the Kherson region ended on the night of November 1 after Russia refused to extend it, and Russian forces resumed attacks on the region on November 2, Ukrainian authorities said, according to RFE/RL.

U.S. Central Command pushed back on Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's claim that Iran has not attacked civilians in neighboring countries, saying Iranian attacks have killed more than 20 civilian mariners in recent months.

items.h: U.S. warns Gulf allies of possible Iran strikes as soon as November 4, report says
items.fact: MS NOW, citing three senior Gulf Arab officials, reported that Washington warned Gulf allies that a brief but intense round of strikes on Iran could come as early as November 4, the day after the midterm elections; the White House said it does not comment on military plans. President Trump told reporters at Mar-a-Lago in Florida on October 31 that one or two of Iran's remaining nuclear-related sites still had to be dealt with, "but we can do that in 10 minutes."

items.h: Araghchi says new proposal cuts Hormuz reopening to two days as Doha talks hit day three
items.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera on October 31 that Iran had drawn up a proposal with Qatari mediators that would shorten the timeline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz to two days. Iran's negotiators held a third straight day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha on November 1, and Araghchi said no final conclusion had yet been reached.

items.h: Mojtaba Khamenei orders forces to answer any threat immediately, without geographic limits
items.fact: Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, ordered the armed forces in an October 31 statement to meet any threat with an immediate, effective response unrestricted by geography, AFP reported. Army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia warned on state TV on November 1 that a new war could last longer than the last one.

items.h: Tanker struck off Saudi coast; Revolutionary Guards claim two tankers hit mines in Hormuz
